top.title: UCTH: Group presses for immediate CMD advert
top.description: …alleges plot to install acting head …Ikpeme dismisses claim as “falsehood” By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR A socio-political group, Good Governance Initiative (GGI), has accused the management of the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) of stalling the recruitment of a new Chief Medical Director (CMD), alleging a scheme to install an acting head and ease in a preferred successor. The Chief Medical Director, Prof. Ikpeme Ikpeme, has rejected the allegation. GGI’s Convener, Mr Bassey Okoi, made the demand in a statement in Calabar on Wednesday, calling for the immediate advertisement of the position, which falls vacant on April 16, 2027, when Ikpeme’s second tenure ends. Okoi said the vacancy should have been advertised in national newspapers six months before the incumbent’s tenure expires. The group had expected the process to start on November 1, he said, but there was no sign of it. He alleged that the delay was meant to tilt the succession in favour of a candidate from Cross River’s southern senatorial district. Okoi insisted that the central senatorial district should produce the next CMD under a long-standing zoning arrangement among the three senatorial districts. He recalled that Prof. Thomas Agan, from the northern district, served eight years before the office moved to the south. According to him, allowing the central district to produce the next CMD is the fairest course, and the incumbent appears determined to disrupt the arrangement. He stressed that zoning was not meant to undermine competence but to promote fairness, inclusiveness and a sense of belonging. He warned that manipulating the process could cause tension and damage institutional harmony. Okoi urged the Federal Ministry of Health to ensure that the recruitment was transparent, credible and consistent with regulations. He also appealed to stakeholders to back an equitable process, saying no individual or interest group should predetermine the outcome. When contacted, Prof. Ikpeme dismissed the claims and said he had already begun the process of appointing his successor ahead of time. He advised the group’s sponsors to stop wasting energy on what he called falsehood and to draw up a programme for taking the hospital to the next level instead. He said the group should take its concerns to the Federal Ministry of Health, the appropriate authority on such appointments. Pointing to the reforms he had carried out to reposition the hospital, Ikpeme said he was no party to the dispute. “I am not a contestant,” he said. top.title: Valley Vista girls basketball gets consolation in Thanksgiving tournament
top.description: Valley Vista, the defending state 6A girls high school basketball champions, hosted its first Thanksgiving girls basketball tournament on Nov. 23-24 at Surprise. The Monsoon took home a consolation prize in the eight-team annual event. Miami took first place, improving to 5-0 on the young season after sweeping four tournament games, winning three of those games by double-digit margins, including a win over Copper Canyon in the title game. Valley Vista defeated Copper Canyon, 49-42, and Ironwood, 34-31, on Monday. Valley trailed Ironwood for three quarters but scored 13 points in the fourth to pull out a victory. The Monsoon are in their first season under new coach MJ Walker. However, Tuesday was not the same story. Valley lost to Copper Canyon in a Round 2 rematch, knocking it out of championship contention. The Monsoon then played Sunrise Mountain in the third-place game and won, 53-51. Freshman Anasophia Rintoul was the star player for Valley Vista, swishing 3-pointers and dishing out assists both days. Senior Braylin Shaw, a returning member from last season's 6A title team, and freshman Mikayla Voll made their presence known, Voll particularly impressive on the boards. Rintoul averaged of 12 points, four rebounds, and four assists in the tournament. Shaw averaged 13 points. top.title: Bayern confirm Musiala’s neurological symptoms began in 2025, pledge recovery support
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management have reaffirmed their support for the midfielder’s recovery and clarified that he was first examined for neurological symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they appeared. In a joint statement after talks on Tuesday, the club and 11WINS, the agency representing Musiala, said: “Both sides agree that the player’s health comes first. Jamal Musiala has their full support on his road to recovery.” Addressing speculation about the midfielder’s health, they added: “Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025. This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical department immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.” The statement said Bayern and Musiala’s management had agreed to continue discussions “in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality”. Musiala has said he was diagnosed with “easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction” after collapsing twice in four days during pre-season. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl described Tuesday’s meeting as “very, very constructive” and said the club’s priority was helping Musiala return after a muscle injury sustained during the international break. “That’s the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something,” Eberl said. The talks follow debate over the Germany international’s form and his contract, which runs until 2030. Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen had questioned the lucrative extension if Musiala did not return to his best, while former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal might need to be renegotiated. Players’ union FIFPRO criticised the club’s public comments, saying an injury or dip in form was no reason to reopen agreed contract terms. Honorary president Uli Hoeness had said Musiala might never regain his previous performance level. Musiala has made five appearances this season, scoring twice. top.title: Smallest school, biggest roar: Redding Christian wins best fan section
top.description: Redding Christian School might have the smallest student population in the Redding area with 150 students at the high school level, but one thing is for certain: Lions fans always show up. In a poll against eight other local high schools , some with over 1,000 students, Redding Christian came through with 2,787 votes (39.9%) to claim the Record Searchlight’s 2026 best fan section honor. “It’s a special atmosphere; it’s one of the best around,” Lions football coach and athletic director Gerald Piper said. “They’re loud, they’re supportive and we couldn’t ask for anything better from our fans.” Volunteer Field at Redding Christian’s Palo Cedro campus is unlike most other high school fields in the area. There’s not a lot of seating available in the bleachers, so to compensate, many fans bring their own seating arrangements and line up along the track next to the field to watch the football team compete on Friday nights. More: High school football | Northern Section championship previews, predictions Some VIPs even drive their vehicles onto the track and set up mini watch parties during games. “I think we have a really cool atmosphere, and a lot of it is the way we’re able to sit along the track here and get really close to the field,” Piper said. It creates a more intimate vibe on Friday nights. Fans who show up early enough to get a seat near midfield can sometimes hear discussions between players and coaches throughout the game, that is when the crowd isn’t too loud. “We don’t have a huge student section, but all the fans come out and support us even when the games aren’t super close and not super entertaining,” senior quarterback Wyatt Shaw said. “The fans still come out and enjoy watching and really cheer us on.” The Lions haven’t given their fans many close games. In nine games played throughout the 2026 season, Redding Christian has outscored opponents 477-53. Regardless, they give their fans a show. The Lions haven't lost on their home field since Sept. 13, 2024. When the football team traveled down to Southern California last year for the 2025 CIF Division 7-AA state championship game — over 500 miles away from home — the Redding Christian fans traveled to support their team. “I was shocked last year when I looked up in our stands and saw how many people made the trip and came down,” Piper said. “Middle schoolers, high schoolers, parents; I thought we’d bring a few, but not as many as we did, so that was awesome.” The Lions made the trip worth it as they claimed their first CIF state title in program history . Yet, the fans show up to more than just football games. Over the past year, Redding Christian has had multiple teams across various sports compete in championship games. Both the boys and girls basketball teams won Northern Section titles during the 2025-26 season, and they both made it to the NorCal regional championship game. top.title: AI can do the calculations. Theoretical physicists are figuring out what comes next.
top.description: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. Read full article Comments

top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Winnipeg Jets begin a three-game road trip Wednesday against the Boston Bruins before visiting the New York Islanders on Friday and the New Jersey Devils on Saturday. The Jets have gone 8-1-1 over their past 10 games, but they’re still sixth in the Central Division despite their impressive turnaround. Playing three road games in four days will force Scott Arniel to make some decisions about how he divides the workload between Stuart Skinner and Nico Daws. After watching Skinner’s performance against the Utah Mammoth on Monday, I’d be tempted to give him a little more responsibility over the next few days. The Jets might have an opportunity to get their No. 1 goalie on a roll at a time when they desperately need to make up ground in the Central Division. The Jets Should Give Skinner a Chance to Build Momentum Skinner stopped 34 of the 36 shots he faced against Utah on Monday, including 25 consecutive shots after allowing two goals in the first period. The Jets were outshot 25-7 over the final 40 minutes, and Skinner deserves a ton of credit for getting them out of that game with two points. The biggest thing I’ve wanted to see from Skinner since he arrived in Winnipeg is consistency. We know he’s capable of stealing games, but we’ve also seen stretches throughout his career where he’s struggled to put together a string of good performances. When he plays as well as he did Monday, I want to see the Jets get him right back in the net and give him a chance to carry that confidence into his next start. I’d give him the start against Boston and, if he plays well, go back to him Friday against the Islanders before turning to Daws against New Jersey on Saturday. There’s value in keeping both goalies involved, but I’d much rather see the Jets come out of this road trip with a confident No. 1 goalie than worry about distributing starts evenly. The Jets have spent much of November digging themselves out of an early-season hole. If Skinner can start playing consistently well behind a team that’s finally finding its footing, Winnipeg could make up quite a bit of ground over the next month. top.title: Panthers Have Been Good. Now, Barkov & Marchand Return
top.description: FORT LAUDERDALE — There have been a lot of big trades in the NHL over the past few weeks but Paul Maurice says the Florida Panthers are making a big deal of their own with captain Sasha Barkov poised to join the lineup tonight. “Big trades around the league,’’ Maurice said, “and I think we made the biggest one. We get Barkov for nothing. Great deal.” Throw the return of Brad Marchand into the mix perhaps tonight against Ottawa as well and the Panthers are looking pretty, pretty good. ”Last year, he was our leading scorer,’’ Maurice said, referencing Marchand’s numbers before he was pulled in March. “He almost gets forgotten, but our offensive numbers are under where we would like them to be without him there.’’ The Panthers certainly have not set the NHL on fire through their first 24 games, but they have more than held their own. Florida comes into tonight’s game against the Senators holding the final wild-card spot in the Eastern Conference and sit three points back from the Canadiens — who just traded for Dylan Larkin — for third in the Atlantic Division. A win against Ottawa tonight would give Florida its third straight divisional win after a 0-4 start. ”I thought we have done a good job to this point in the season,” said Brady Tkachuk , who faces the Senators for the second time since his blockbuster summer trade to the Panthers. “With everyone, there is room to grow, always room to get better. But it has just been a blast to be here with this group, learning from so many guys, the coaches, the staff, everyone. I’m having a time right now.” The Panthers, certainly, will be getting a boost with the return of Barkov and Marchand. Although Maurice would not commit to Barkov and/or Marchand rejoining the lineup tonight, he has been hinting at it for the past couple of days. The Panthers have also cleared the salary cap path for Barkov’s return off LTIR first by placing Cole Reinhardt on waivers Sunday — with the second cap shoe dropping Tuesday with Cole Schwindt waived. Barkov missed all of last season with a right knee injury, then hurt his left one in his second game back on Oct. 1 in San Jose. Marchand was shut down at the end of last season, needed surgery in August, but made a quick return to the lineup only to hurt his left knee in the middle of his second game back. The Panthers are happy to have them back — and would love to see them stick around a little longer this time around. “There’s an excitement for me and it is long-term for them as well,’’ Maurice said. “What we look like (Wednesday) night, it won’t be a switch that you can flip back. You miss that much hockey … but (Barkov) is one of the best players in the world. We just haven’t had him here for a year and a half.” Said Tkachuk: “It gives us such a boost. It feels like they haven’t missed a beat out there.’’ ON DECK: GAME No. 25 OTTAWA SENATORS at FLORIDA PANTHERS When: Wednesday, 7 p.m. Where: Amerant Bank Arena, Sunrise Local TV: Scripps Sports — WSFL 39 (Miami/FTL); WHDT 9

top.title: Watford appoint Iordanescu as head coach
top.description: Edward Iordanescu took Romania to the last 16 at Euro 2024 [Getty Images] Watford have appointed former Romania boss Edward Iordanescu as the Championship club's new head coach. The 48-year-old replaces Alessio Dionisi, who was sacked on Sunday after only five months in charge following a run of seven defeats in their past 10 league games, culminating in Saturday's 4-0 loss to Sheffield United. "I am very proud and happy to be at this football club," Iordanescu told the club website. "I can see the team is in a difficult moment but I have already watched many of the games over the last few days and I'm very confident about the future." He becomes Watford's sixth new boss in less than 18 months and is the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012. Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford The former CFR Cluj and Legia Warsaw manager will be joined at Watford by backroom staff Alexandru Radu, Grzegorz Mokry and Michele Iannucci, but will watch Wednesday's Championship match at home to Blackburn Rovers from the stands before taking charge for Saturday's game at Derby. Adrian Mariappa will oversee Wednesday's match at Vicarage Road (19:45 GMT), alongside Paul Furlong and Lloyd Doyley. The Watford job is Iordanescu's first since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025, where he won the Super Cup last season. It is the 10th managerial post of his 15-year coaching career, which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj - who he guided to the Romanian title and two domestic cups after joining midway through the 2020-21 season. He also spent two-and-a-half years in charge of Romania, guiding them to the last 16 of Euro 2024, where they were beaten by the Netherlands. Iordanescu takes over a Watford side currently three points above the relegation zone , having won only four of their 16 games so far. Who is Iordanescu and what is he facing? Watford will be Iordanescu's first job in English football [Getty Images] Although untried in English football, Watford are getting a trophy-winning head coach with a wide-ranging CV spanning spells in his homeland, Bulgaria and Poland, as well as elite-level international experience with Romania. His connections with his national side run deep as the son of his country's legendary former head coach Anghel Iordanescu, who famously took them to the quarter-finals of the 1994 World Cup during a reign of more than 100 games. It is likely he will need every bit of that nous and inspiration as he becomes the latest boss to try to revive a club which continues to plough through managers at an alarming rate. Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, with Iordanescu becoming the sixth permanent boss since Tom Cleverley was sacked in May 2025. top.title: Lincoln sack head coach duo Cohen and Shaw
top.description: Chris Cohen (left) and Tom Shaw had been on the coaching staff together at Lincoln for a number of years before they got the top job together [Shutterstock] Lincoln City have sacked their head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side. The pair departed a little over 12 hours after they oversaw a 4-0 defeat at fellow strugglers Charlton Athletic on Tuesday. The loss leaves the Imps just three points above the relegation places in what is the club's first season back in the second tier for 65 years. Cohen and Shaw were assistant coaches under Michael Skubala when Lincoln were promoted as League One title winners last season. They were surprisingly promoted to replace their boss as a managerial double act. Charlton brush aside outclassed Lincoln What next for Lincoln City after coach duo exit? The duo oversaw just four wins from 17 league games this season, and Tuesday's loss at The Valley was their fifth in succession and heaviest since being thumped 6-0 by West Ham in mid-October. Lincoln's chairman Ron Fowler, the American billionaire who took a controlling stake in the club when they were on their way to promotion last season, said the decision to sack the pair was in the "best interests" of the Imps. "We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division," he told the club website. First-team coach Shaun Pearson will take charge of Lincoln, with the support of Paul McShane and David Preece, on an interim basis. Lincoln are next in action on Saturday when they host high-flying Wolves. When Cohen and Shaw got the job at Sincil Bank it came somewhat as a shock because managing football teams in tandem is somewhat of a curiosity in the game. Liverpool famously did with Gerard Houllier and Roy Evans in 1998 when the partnership lasted six months as results slumped, while Tottenham gave it a go with Doug Livermore and Ray Clemence earlier that same decade. The hope was that the Cohen-Shaw show would be a lot more like Coventry's success story under John Sillett and George Curtis, who guided the Sky Blues to FA Cup glory in 1987. Lincoln's decision-makers were proactive in talking up their decision, with sporting director Jez George explaining in June that the appointment "wasn't a case of do the easy thing, but it was absolutely the right thing for the club". Shaw and Cohen were also quizzed at length about how the joint role would work, starting with "who's going to make the subs?" Cohen was upfront when he said "from the outside looking in, it's not normal", but the former Nottingham Forest and West Ham midfielder insisted that the job share was "really normal" to them. How peculiar it might have looked, or how the dynamics between the pair worked, all become somewhat irrelevant in recent weeks as Lincoln's dire run of form has plunged them towards the relegation places. nigeria.description: …alleges plot to install acting head …Ikpeme dismisses claim as “falsehood” By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR A socio-political group, Good Governance Initiative (GGI), has accused the management of the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) of stalling the recruitment of a new Chief Medical Director (CMD), alleging a scheme to install an acting head and ease in a preferred successor. The Chief Medical Director, Prof. Ikpeme Ikpeme, has rejected the allegation. GGI’s Convener, Mr Bassey Okoi, made the demand in a statement in Calabar on Wednesday, calling for the immediate advertisement of the position, which falls vacant on April 16, 2027, when Ikpeme’s second tenure ends. Okoi said the vacancy should have been advertised in national newspapers six months before the incumbent’s tenure expires. The group had expected the process to start on November 1, he said, but there was no sign of it. He alleged that the delay was meant to tilt the succession in favour of a candidate from Cross River’s southern senatorial district. Okoi insisted that the central senatorial district should produce the next CMD under a long-standing zoning arrangement among the three senatorial districts. He recalled that Prof. Thomas Agan, from the northern district, served eight years before the office moved to the south. According to him, allowing the central district to produce the next CMD is the fairest course, and the incumbent appears determined to disrupt the arrangement. He stressed that zoning was not meant to undermine competence but to promote fairness, inclusiveness and a sense of belonging. He warned that manipulating the process could cause tension and damage institutional harmony. Okoi urged the Federal Ministry of Health to ensure that the recruitment was transparent, credible and consistent with regulations. He also appealed to stakeholders to back an equitable process, saying no individual or interest group should predetermine the outcome. When contacted, Prof. Ikpeme dismissed the claims and said he had already begun the process of appointing his successor ahead of time. He advised the group’s sponsors to stop wasting energy on what he called falsehood and to draw up a programme for taking the hospital to the next level instead. He said the group should take its concerns to the Federal Ministry of Health, the appropriate authority on such appointments. Pointing to the reforms he had carried out to reposition the hospital, Ikpeme said he was no party to the dispute. “I am not a contestant,” he said. nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management have reaffirmed their support for the midfielder’s recovery and clarified that he was first examined for neurological symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they appeared. In a joint statement after talks on Tuesday, the club and 11WINS, the agency representing Musiala, said: “Both sides agree that the player’s health comes first. Jamal Musiala has their full support on his road to recovery.” Addressing speculation about the midfielder’s health, they added: “Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025. This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical department immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.” The statement said Bayern and Musiala’s management had agreed to continue discussions “in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality”. Musiala has said he was diagnosed with “easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction” after collapsing twice in four days during pre-season. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl described Tuesday’s meeting as “very, very constructive” and said the club’s priority was helping Musiala return after a muscle injury sustained during the international break. “That’s the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something,” Eberl said. The talks follow debate over the Germany international’s form and his contract, which runs until 2030. Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen had questioned the lucrative extension if Musiala did not return to his best, while former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal might need to be renegotiated. Players’ union FIFPRO criticised the club’s public comments, saying an injury or dip in form was no reason to reopen agreed contract terms. Honorary president Uli Hoeness had said Musiala might never regain his previous performance level. Musiala has made five appearances this season, scoring twice. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s $54bn external reserves cover 10 months’ imports – Cardoso
nigeria.description: The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Olayemi Cardoso, says Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at 54.02 billion dollars as of Nov. 17, sufficient to cover 10.26 months of imports for goods and services. Cardoso said this in Abuja while presenting the communique from the 308th meeting of the apex bank’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on Tuesday. He said that headline inflation year-on-year declined further to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September, driven by both food and core components. “Core inflation eased further to 10.78 per cent in October 2026 from 12.95 per cent in September, driven mainly by housing, education services, and insurance and financial services. “This reflects the impact of the restrictive monetary policy stance and sustained stability in the foreign exchange market. “Similarly, food inflation declined to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent as prices of processed food and farm produce moderated following the commencement of the harvest season. “The Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) sustained its expansion to 53.2 index points in October from 53 index points in September, driven by improved activity in the industrial, agricultural, and services sectors.” Cardoso said that global economic growth was projected to moderate in 2026 before regaining momentum in 2027. According to him, the slowdown reflects the combined effects of elevated energy prices, persistent trade policy uncertainty, and diminishing fiscal space. “Nonetheless, robust investment in artificial intelligence and other technology-related sectors alongside its broad-based adoption is expected to partly offset the impact of these headwinds. “Global price pressures continue to intensify in 2026 but are expected to ease progressively in 2027. “Risks to the outlook, however, remain tilted to the upside, arising from persistent energy and supply chain disruptions, vulnerability to cyberattacks, elevated commodity and freight costs, as well as increasing global trade fragmentation,” he said. He said that the outlook for the domestic economy remained positive for the rest of 2026 and into 2027, supported by improved crude oil production and sustained expansion in agriculture, services, and industrial activity. “The continued expansion of the Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index in October further signals positive growth momentum. “Disinflation is also expected to be sustained over the short to medium term on the back of the restrictive stance of monetary policy, continued stability in the foreign exchange market, and improved food supply. “Nevertheless, key risks to the inflation outlook remain the continued disruption to global energy supplies and adverse weather conditions. “Overall, the committee remained optimistic about the outlook for the domestic economy, supported by resilient output growth, moderating inflationary pressures, stronger external buffers, and continued soundness of the financial system,” he said. nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The European Union (EU) and its member states, under Team Europe, have launched a €100,000 (about ₦152.9 million) emergency fund to support women facing gender-based threats and violence linked to political and electoral participation ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Ireland’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Lesley Ní Bhriain, announced the launch of the Rapid Response Fund on Political and Election-Related Gender-Based Violence at a meeting in Abuja on Tuesday. Ní Bhriain said the fund, which would operate from November 2026 to March 2027, was designed to provide urgent assistance to eligible women facing threats or harm because of their involvement in political and electoral activities. She said it could also support women facing credible and imminent threats before further harm occurred. According to her, women should be able to contest elections, campaign, vote, organise, observe elections and report on electoral activities without fear of intimidation or violence. She said the initiative was established to protect and assist women, stressing that it would not be used to finance election campaigns. “Today, Team Europe in Nigeria launches the Rapid Response Fund on Political and Election-related Gender-based Violence, with an indicative value of approximately N152.9 million Naira, equivalent to EUR 100,000,” she said. “No woman should have to recount personal experience publicly, give an interview or appear in a photograph to receive assistance,” she added. The ambassador directed women seeking assistance to contact HerStoryOurStory on 0806 429 2526 or through herstoryourstoryng@gmail.com, saying the organisation would handle requests for support. She said the fund would also strengthen the capacity of service providers to respond promptly to urgent cases, with women’s safety, dignity and choices guiding its administration. Ní Bhriain urged political parties and their leaders to prevent intimidation, harassment and violence, while calling on relevant authorities to protect women at risk, investigate reported offences and ensure survivors had access to justice. She also urged women’s organisations and female political leaders to publicise the initiative, refer women to support services and help coordinate responses to emergencies. The ambassador warned that online threats and harassment could extend beyond victims to affect their families and undermine their participation in public life. She called on the media to protect survivors’ identities and provide accurate information on how women could access assistance. nigeria.title: ‘Detty December: 7 rules everyone should follow before going out’
nigeria.description: A TikTok user, Evelyn, has shared a list of rules for Detty December and beyond, advising people to prioritise personal hygiene, safety and proper planning when attending social events during the festive season. In a video posted on TikTok, Evelyn outlined seven rules she expects people to follow when going out, noting that the hot weather, transportation arrangements and possible security concerns should be considered. She advised people to use deodorants with at least 48-hour protection, joking that the weather was already hot and people should not make the situation worse for others. On financial preparedness, she urged revellers to carry both physical cash and mobile money, recommending that they have at least 500 in both payment options to avoid difficulties when making transactions. Evelyn also encouraged people to purchase event tickets ahead of time, particularly when relying on contact persons who might not be dependable. She further advised attendees to respect event dress codes and avoid wearing outfits she described as excessive. Addressing security concerns, she warned people against concealing potentially problematic items from their companions, saying anyone found with such items during a police stop should take responsibility for their actions. She also recommended having at least two emergency contacts and carrying some form of personal protection for unforeseen situations. The TikTok user concluded by warning against unnecessary confrontations, saying she would not participate in fights simply because someone in her group had picked an argument. Her rules come as Nigerians prepare for the festive season, popularly known as Detty December, which is characterised by concerts, parties, social gatherings and other entertainment activities. nigeria.title: C/River imposes curfew on Iso-Bendeghe, Boje over deadly land clashes
nigeria.description: .bans entry into disputed areas, orders security agencies to enforce order By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Government has imposed an immediate dusk-to-dawn curfew on Iso-Bendeghe and Boje communities in Boki Local Government Area, following protracted clashes over a land dispute between the two neighbours. The curfew, announced Wednesday in a statement by the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Pst. Ekpenyong Cobham, will last one week from November 24, 2026. Cobham said the measure became necessary because the crisis was threatening the peace of the area. “This has become necessary as the situation has continued to threaten lives, property and peace in the area,” he said. Under the order, no movement is allowed in either community from 6 pm to 6 am daily. The statement also barred residents of both communities from entering or moving into the disputed areas “for any reason.” Security agencies were directed to enforce the curfew strictly. The government warned that violators would face the full weight of the law. “Defaulters will be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law,” the Commissioner said. The state government appealed to community leaders, youths and other stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign. It said it remained committed to ending the hostilities between the two communities. “This administration remains committed to restoring lasting peace between the two communities and appeals to leaders, youths and all stakeholders in Iso-Bendeghe and Boje to embrace dialogue and allow peace to reign,” the statement said. Cobham added that the government would keep a close watch on developments in the area. “The government will continue to monitor the situation closely until normalcy returns in the area,” he said. nigeria.title: CAF releases finalists for 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award (Full list)
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has released the five finalists for the 2026 Men’s Player of the Year award, with reigning winner Achraf Hakimi, Senegal’s Sadio Mané and three other players making the shortlist. The final nominees were selected from an initial list of 10 players based on their performances for club and country during the period under consideration. Morocco has three representatives on the list, while Senegal has two, reflecting the countries’ strong performances in the period. Hakimi, who plays for French champions Paris Saint-Germain, is seeking to retain the award after helping the club win the UEFA Champions League and French Ligue 1 title. The Moroccan defender also captained his national team during its campaigns at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Mané, a two-time winner of the award in 2019 and 2022, is also in contention for a third title after helping Senegal win the 2025 AFCON. The Al-Nassr forward was named the tournament’s Best Player in recognition of his leadership and contributions to Senegal’s triumph. Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz earned a place on the shortlist following his performances for Morocco, particularly at the 2025 AFCON, where he won the Golden Boot with five goals. Villarreal midfielder Pape Gueye also made the list after scoring the winning goal in extra time as Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the AFCON final in Rabat. His performances at the tournament also earned him a place in the Best XI. Completing the shortlist is Morocco’s Ismael Saibari, who played an important role in his country’s run to the AFCON final, including scoring against Cameroon in the quarter-finals. The winner will be announced at the 2026 CAF Awards ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, December 2, at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, popularly known as the National Theatre, in Lagos. The ceremony is expected to begin at 7pm Nigerian time. The CAF Awards will return to Lagos for the first time since the 2014 edition. nigeria.title: Meta unveils $700,000 AI grant for Nigerian startups
nigeria.description: By Juliet Umeh Meta has announced a $700,000 artificial intelligence (AI) grant programme for startups and developers in Nigeria and six other countries, as part of efforts to accelerate AI innovation and expand access to emerging technologies. The programme, scheduled to commence in 2027, will cover Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates (UAE), according to a statement issued by the company on Tuesday. Meta said the grant would support startups and developers building solutions using its AI tools and wearable technologies. The company also announced the launch of a new hub designed to provide educational resources and information on its AI developments, partnerships and innovation initiatives across Africa, the Middle East and Turkey. The hub will operate through three learning programmes: AI Academy, AI Literacy and AI for Small and Medium-sized Businesses. The programmes are designed for students, developers, entrepreneurs and business professionals, with Meta targeting more than five million beneficiaries across the three regions over the next three years. Meta’s Vice-President of Public Policy for Africa, the Middle East and Turkey, Kojo Boakye, said the initiatives were designed to equip developers and entrepreneurs with the skills, resources and support needed to build AI solutions that address challenges in their communities. “AI’s value will be judged by the real impact it has on people’s lives,” Boakye said. “Across our region, people are building solutions around the languages they speak, the businesses they run and the challenges their communities face. “The Impact Grant and Hub are about giving more builders the support, skills and resources to turn those ideas into useful products and services. We want people here to help shape AI’s future, not simply use what others have built.” In another initiative, Meta announced the AMET AI Awards 2026, with more than $100,000 in prizes across seven categories to recognise outstanding AI innovations. The company said the awards would recognise finalists from its AI Academy and Wearables Studio programmes, including students, developers and startups. The award categories include Wearables Innovation of the Year, AI Builder of the Year, Emerging Innovator of the Year and Startup of the Year. Others are AI for Accessibility and Inclusion, AI for Social and Economic Impact, and People’s Choice, which will be decided through a live vote by attendees at the summit. Meta said the awards would recognise projects leveraging AI-powered technologies to address everyday needs, improve access to opportunities and services, and promote social and economic development. nigeria.title: Zamfara: Bandits kill two headmasters, 13 others, abduct residents
nigeria.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Armed bandits have killed 15 people, including two primary school headmasters and an 11-month-old baby, in separate attacks on communities in Zamfara State. The attacks, which occurred in Tungan Janbuzu and Madanbaji communities, also left several residents abducted, according to a report by the BBC Hausa Service. The two headmasters, identified as Kabiru Salisu and Shehu Umar, both aged 35, were reportedly killed in an ambush at Janbuzu. A resident of the community, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the incident occurred at about 4pm, following the escape of some kidnapped residents from their captors. He explained that the bandits had earlier abducted some locals from Janbuzu and kept them in captivity, forcing them to work for their captors. According to him, the kidnappers had demanded a ransom of N300,000, which was subsequently delivered to them at a location near Kiawa. He said the bandits collected the money but later drove the person who delivered it away, claiming that the payment was meant for recharge cards and fuel. The resident further narrated that the bandits had taken six captives into the bush, tied them up and left them under the supervision of a young boy while they went to Aboro to purchase drugs and other supplies. However, the captives reportedly managed to untie themselves, overpower their guard, seize his gun and escape after beating him. The resident said the escape angered other members of the gang, who were reportedly hiding on a nearby farm. He said the armed men subsequently ambushed the two headmasters near a location known as Gora, seized their mobile phones and shot them dead. The resident, however, said kidnapping incidents had reduced considerably in the area, except in communities located close to the forests and bushes where the bandits operate. He expressed concern over the continued vulnerability of residents in remote settlements, despite the reported reduction in kidnapping incidents. Morka said anyone accused of rigging an election should be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law, rather than subjected to punishment determined by political parties or their supporters. The APC spokesman spoke on News Central on Wednesday while reacting to allegations of violence by NDC supporters against members of the ruling party. His comments followed remarks by the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, who had defended the slogan during an interview with Channels Television after the party’s town hall meeting in Taraba State on Tuesday. Obi had dismissed concerns over the message, insisting that the supporters were opposed to election rigging, not political campaigns. “They said we said ‘rig and die.’ We didn’t say ‘campaign and die.’ What we, people said is that they don’t want rigging this time. They didn’t say they don’t want campaign this time. If anything, they want campaign this time,” Obi said. However, reacting to the explanation, Morka said the slogan was inflammatory and questioned the implication of allowing individuals to determine who had rigged an election and should therefore die. “Now, what does that mean? What message are you sending when you appoint yourself as custodians of elections, and therefore anyone you consider to have rigged an election — because that’s a subjective standard — should die,” he said. Morka said he had watched a video in which Obi defended the statement, adding that the NDC candidate had acknowledged that the message was “rig and die” rather than “campaign and die”. The APC spokesman then challenged Obi and the NDC to explain the legal justification for such a position. “So, if somebody rigs an election, since when did Nigerian law prescribe the death penalty for rigging an election?” he asked. Morka maintained that anyone suspected of electoral malpractice should be apprehended and made to face the consequences provided by law. “I think as a lawyer and as a citizen, that anyone who rigs an election should be apprehended and be made to face the law as provided by the law, not as provided by Peter Obi or the NDC stalwarts who make this very incendiary comment,” he said. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). Veteran Nollywood actor Chief Dr Pete Edochie and his wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, at a church service. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Chief Dr Pete Edochie is survived by his beloved wife of over five decades, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, their six children—Leo, Adam, Linc, Jean, Yul, and Eva Edochie (with Linc and Yul following closely in his acting footsteps)—as well as his siblings, grandchildren, and extended family. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. entertainment.description: For many people, buying property is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make. Yet, knowing who to trust, how to verify ownership and whether a property is worth the investment can make the process overwhelming. It is a challenge Solape Fayemi hopes to address with the launch of Saina Properties , a real estate company now operating across Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States and the United Arab Emirates. Officially unveiled at an event held on 17 November at the Marriott Hotel, Ikeja GRA, Lagos, Saina Properties is built around a simple idea: property ownership should be guided by sound advice, proper verification and professional support, not just the excitement of closing a deal. For Solape, whose experience in the investment industry shaped her understanding of money, risk and wealth creation, the decision to establish the company came from recognising the need for a more considered approach to real estate. “We are not building Saina Properties because the world needs another company selling properties. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. sports.title: Panthers Have Been Good. Now, Barkov & Marchand Return
sports.description: FORT LAUDERDALE — There have been a lot of big trades in the NHL over the past few weeks but Paul Maurice says the Florida Panthers are making a big deal of their own with captain Sasha Barkov poised to join the lineup tonight. “Big trades around the league,’’ Maurice said, “and I think we made the biggest one. We get Barkov for nothing. Great deal.” Throw the return of Brad Marchand into the mix perhaps tonight against Ottawa as well and the Panthers are looking pretty, pretty good. ”Last year, he was our leading scorer,’’ Maurice said, referencing Marchand’s numbers before he was pulled in March. “He almost gets forgotten, but our offensive numbers are under where we would like them to be without him there.’’ The Panthers certainly have not set the NHL on fire through their first 24 games, but they have more than held their own. Florida comes into tonight’s game against the Senators holding the final wild-card spot in the Eastern Conference and sit three points back from the Canadiens — who just traded for Dylan Larkin — for third in the Atlantic Division. A win against Ottawa tonight would give Florida its third straight divisional win after a 0-4 start. ”I thought we have done a good job to this point in the season,” said Brady Tkachuk , who faces the Senators for the second time since his blockbuster summer trade to the Panthers. “With everyone, there is room to grow, always room to get better. But it has just been a blast to be here with this group, learning from so many guys, the coaches, the staff, everyone. I’m having a time right now.” The Panthers, certainly, will be getting a boost with the return of Barkov and Marchand. Although Maurice would not commit to Barkov and/or Marchand rejoining the lineup tonight, he has been hinting at it for the past couple of days. The Panthers have also cleared the salary cap path for Barkov’s return off LTIR first by placing Cole Reinhardt on waivers Sunday — with the second cap shoe dropping Tuesday with Cole Schwindt waived. Barkov missed all of last season with a right knee injury, then hurt his left one in his second game back on Oct. 1 in San Jose. Marchand was shut down at the end of last season, needed surgery in August, but made a quick return to the lineup only to hurt his left knee in the middle of his second game back. The Panthers are happy to have them back — and would love to see them stick around a little longer this time around. “There’s an excitement for me and it is long-term for them as well,’’ Maurice said. “What we look like (Wednesday) night, it won’t be a switch that you can flip back. You miss that much hockey … but (Barkov) is one of the best players in the world. We just haven’t had him here for a year and a half.” Said Tkachuk: “It gives us such a boost. It feels like they haven’t missed a beat out there.’’ ON DECK: GAME No. 25 OTTAWA SENATORS at FLORIDA PANTHERS When: Wednesday, 7 p.m. Where: Amerant Bank Arena, Sunrise Local TV: Scripps Sports — WSFL 39 (Miami/FTL); WHDT 9

The English giants, who finished third last campaign, are 19th in the table at the moment, and new manager Mauricio Pochettino is staring ahead at a huge challenge. He failed to cement a place in the starting XI at St. James’ Park, spending much of his time away on loan. The Englishman eventually joined Peterborough United in 2018, before joining Brentford in the summer of 2020. It was at the Brentford Community Stadium that Toney earned the reputation of a proven marksman, scoring 72 goals and setting up 23 more in 141 appearances. sports.title: Watford appoint Iordanescu as head coach
sports.description: Edward Iordanescu took Romania to the last 16 at Euro 2024 [Getty Images] Watford have appointed former Romania boss Edward Iordanescu as the Championship club's new head coach. The 48-year-old replaces Alessio Dionisi, who was sacked on Sunday after only five months in charge following a run of seven defeats in their past 10 league games, culminating in Saturday's 4-0 loss to Sheffield United. "I am very proud and happy to be at this football club," Iordanescu told the club website. "I can see the team is in a difficult moment but I have already watched many of the games over the last few days and I'm very confident about the future." He becomes Watford's sixth new boss in less than 18 months and is the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012. Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford The former CFR Cluj and Legia Warsaw manager will be joined at Watford by backroom staff Alexandru Radu, Grzegorz Mokry and Michele Iannucci, but will watch Wednesday's Championship match at home to Blackburn Rovers from the stands before taking charge for Saturday's game at Derby. Adrian Mariappa will oversee Wednesday's match at Vicarage Road (19:45 GMT), alongside Paul Furlong and Lloyd Doyley. The Watford job is Iordanescu's first since leaving Legia Warsaw in October 2025, where he won the Super Cup last season. It is the 10th managerial post of his 15-year coaching career, which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj - who he guided to the Romanian title and two domestic cups after joining midway through the 2020-21 season. He also spent two-and-a-half years in charge of Romania, guiding them to the last 16 of Euro 2024, where they were beaten by the Netherlands. Iordanescu takes over a Watford side currently three points above the relegation zone , having won only four of their 16 games so far. Who is Iordanescu and what is he facing? Watford will be Iordanescu's first job in English football [Getty Images] Although untried in English football, Watford are getting a trophy-winning head coach with a wide-ranging CV spanning spells in his homeland, Bulgaria and Poland, as well as elite-level international experience with Romania. His connections with his national side run deep as the son of his country's legendary former head coach Anghel Iordanescu, who famously took them to the quarter-finals of the 1994 World Cup during a reign of more than 100 games. It is likely he will need every bit of that nous and inspiration as he becomes the latest boss to try to revive a club which continues to plough through managers at an alarming rate. Dionisi was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, with Iordanescu becoming the sixth permanent boss since Tom Cleverley was sacked in May 2025. sports.title: Lincoln sack head coach duo Cohen and Shaw
sports.description: Chris Cohen (left) and Tom Shaw had been on the coaching staff together at Lincoln for a number of years before they got the top job together [Shutterstock] Lincoln City have sacked their head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side. The pair departed a little over 12 hours after they oversaw a 4-0 defeat at fellow strugglers Charlton Athletic on Tuesday. The loss leaves the Imps just three points above the relegation places in what is the club's first season back in the second tier for 65 years. Cohen and Shaw were assistant coaches under Michael Skubala when Lincoln were promoted as League One title winners last season. They were surprisingly promoted to replace their boss as a managerial double act. Charlton brush aside outclassed Lincoln What next for Lincoln City after coach duo exit? The duo oversaw just four wins from 17 league games this season, and Tuesday's loss at The Valley was their fifth in succession and heaviest since being thumped 6-0 by West Ham in mid-October. Lincoln's chairman Ron Fowler, the American billionaire who took a controlling stake in the club when they were on their way to promotion last season, said the decision to sack the pair was in the "best interests" of the Imps. "We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division," he told the club website. First-team coach Shaun Pearson will take charge of Lincoln, with the support of Paul McShane and David Preece, on an interim basis. Lincoln are next in action on Saturday when they host high-flying Wolves. When Cohen and Shaw got the job at Sincil Bank it came somewhat as a shock because managing football teams in tandem is somewhat of a curiosity in the game. Liverpool famously did with Gerard Houllier and Roy Evans in 1998 when the partnership lasted six months as results slumped, while Tottenham gave it a go with Doug Livermore and Ray Clemence earlier that same decade. The hope was that the Cohen-Shaw show would be a lot more like Coventry's success story under John Sillett and George Curtis, who guided the Sky Blues to FA Cup glory in 1987. Lincoln's decision-makers were proactive in talking up their decision, with sporting director Jez George explaining in June that the appointment "wasn't a case of do the easy thing, but it was absolutely the right thing for the club". Shaw and Cohen were also quizzed at length about how the joint role would work, starting with "who's going to make the subs?" Cohen was upfront when he said "from the outside looking in, it's not normal", but the former Nottingham Forest and West Ham midfielder insisted that the job share was "really normal" to them. How peculiar it might have looked, or how the dynamics between the pair worked, all become somewhat irrelevant in recent weeks as Lincoln's dire run of form has plunged them towards the relegation places. technology.title: AI can do the calculations. Theoretical physicists are figuring out what comes next.
technology.description: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. technology.title: The world's fastest computers have a problem: Keeping the work running
technology.description: Frontier, Oak Ridge National Laboratory's exascale supercomputer, has thousands of processors working together on scientific problems. It also has a surprisingly ordinary way of ruining a researcher's day: one node going down. An uncorrectable memory error can do it, or a maintenance mishap. Scott Atchley , chief technology officer at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility, describes technicians accidentally rebooting the wrong node or risking a neighboring node's power supply while working in tightly packed racks. The hardware fault can affect just one node, but a simulation running across thousands of processors can grind to a halt. Then comes a series of questions. How recently did the application save its progress? How much computation needs repeating? And how long before the scheduler lets the job run again? For operators, the challenge isn't just keeping the supercomputer running. It's keeping the science moving. One bad node and everybody suffers On Frontier , a memory error can have an outsized audience. Atchley says uncorrectable double-bit errors in high-bandwidth memory occurred about 1.5 times a day during the supercomputer's early bring-up. Its predecessor, Summit, saw roughly one every two weeks. This sounds like a backward step, until you count the memory. Frontier has more than 16 times as much, giving bad bits considerably more places to hide. Memory isn't the only problem. Problematic GPU firmware can crash a node, and so can a technician rebooting the wrong one. Interconnect faults add another way for a large job to come unstuck. In a tightly coupled simulation using the Message Passing Interface (MPI) simulation, thousands of processes, or ranks, exchange data and participate in collective operations. If one rank disappears, the others cannot carry on as though nothing happened. Clockwork.io CEO Suresh Vasudevan describes a similar dependency in synchronized GPU training. One failed GPU can bring a 1,024-GPU job to a pause. An underperforming GPU can be almost as troublesome: if one participant runs at 80 percent speed, others might have to spend time waiting for it. The bigger the machine, the more ways there are for one small problem to become everybody's problem. How often should you hit save? Since stopping every component from failing isn't an option, researchers need a way to preserve their work. That's where checkpointing comes in. The application periodically saves its state so that, when something goes wrong, the simulation can resume from an earlier point instead of starting from scratch. The catch is that saving progress costs computing time, and doing it too often can become almost as wasteful as losing the work itself. Vasudevan explains this with an example. If writing a checkpoint takes 30 seconds, saving every five minutes consumes roughly 10 percent of computing time. Stretch that interval to 50 minutes, and the overhead drops to about 1 percent. This case kicked off in 2020, when the US Department of Justice claimed entities Huawei operated in America violated federal law. The indictment led to a trial on a dozen criminal matters that has played out over the last three months in the Eastern District Court of New York. The Department of Justice’s celebration of the decision says Huawei was found to have stolen Cisco’s source code, after prosecutors showed evidence that “Huawei engineers left Cisco’s notes about the Cisco code, referred to Cisco using its name backwards ‘ocsic’ and described that portions of the code remained as they existed in the ‘ocsic’ code.” Another item of evidence apparently showed a Huawei staffer photographing Fujitsu equipment while wearing a fake employee badge for a company called “Weihua” – cunningly reversing the two syllables of “Huawei.” Another allegation the jury accepted involved Huawei staffers signing a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) ahead of a visit to T-Mobile to inspect a robot the telco created to test mobile devices. technology.title: This could mess with Thanksgiving, says VMware as it drops third critical patch bundle in a week
technology.description: VMware has issued its third critical security advisory in a week, this time to warn of four critical flaws and address a total of 23 issues. VMSA-2026-0011 landed on November 24, just five days after two other advisories. VMware’s FAQ for the new advisory includes the following remarks: Because of coordinated disclosure and release pipeline timing this VMSA comes on the heels of VMSA-2026-0009, and atop a major holiday in the United States. The security vulnerability landscape is more dynamic than ever; please know that while we acknowledge this timing is not optimal, your ability to operate and maintain a secure environment amidst modern, AI-assisted threats is paramount to us. Make of that what you will as you ponder how and when to patch the four critical flaws, including the 9.8-rated CVE-2026-123903, which allows a malicious actor to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to vCenter, the management tool VMware users rely on to manage hosts and VMs. This is the third 9.8-rated authentication issue VMware has fixed in vCenter since July. Two of the other critical flaws in this new advisory allow an attacker to run code on an ESX host, earning the bugs a 9.8 rating. CVE-2026-123910 makes that possible thanks to a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the I/O filter service, while CVE-2026-123911 is a use-after-free vulnerability. The other critical flaw, CVE-2026-123912, can result in a guest escape from VMware’s desktop Workstation and Fusion desktop hypervisors. It’s also present in VMware’s ESX hypervisor, but attackers thankfully can’t escape that product’s sandbox. This one’s easy to mitigate because the problem is in a USB controller that users can turn off. Most of the other flaws require installation of updated software. There’s a little good news in that some of the software updates VMware issued last week include fixes for the newly disclosed flaws. But there are still plenty of fresh fixes to apply, across ten products: ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, VMware tools, Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, the Telco Cloud Platform, Telco Cloud Infrastructure, and the VMware Avi Load Balancer. VMware’s advisory thanks external researchers for finding and reporting most of the flaws. The Broadcom business unit is known to be a member of Project Glasswing, the Anthropic-run effort to use the Mythos model to find flaws that has seen many vendors dramatically increase the number of patches they produce. In past years, VMware has often published considerably more than this year’s 11 security advisories. With five weeks left in the year, perhaps vAdmins need to worry Christmas might also get complicated. ®

technology.title: Nutanix CEO announces gradual departure, intent to complete set of storage links
technology.description: Nutanix CEO Rajiv Ramaswami has decided to step down from the job once the company’s board can find his successor. Ramaswami announced his decision on Tuesday and in conversation with The Register said he doesn’t have another job lined up, isn’t sure what he will do next, fancies sitting on boards or advising startups, but will take a break after Nutanix finds its next leader. The CEO moved from VMware to Nutanix in 2020 and characterized his time at the company as writing its “second chapter.” The first, he explained, saw Nutanix focus on hyperconverged infrastructure (HCI) and a limited group of workloads, especially desktop virtualization, while struggling to make a profit. In chapter two, Nutanix redefined HCI as “hybrid cloud infrastructure” by enabling its stack to run on-prem or in public clouds, and by adding support for containers alongside VMs. Ramaswami took credit for stabilizing Nutanix’s finances while leading the expansion of its platform and for keeping net promoter scores high while the company grew. The CEO added that Nutanix’s decision to end its devotion to virtualized storage and start to support external arrays was also part of chapter two. Ramaswami said he hopes to expand the number of storage vendors Nutanix supports beyond Dell, Everpure, and NetApp, until it works with all major array suppliers. Chapter 3, he said, will be making Nutanix an AI platform, “by catering to a whole new set of ecosystems.” Ramaswami told The Register he had been thinking about moving on for some time and raised it with the board in recent weeks. In the letter he wrote to Nutanix staff , the CEO said the company's board has begun the search for a successor and said he will remain at his post until a replacement is found and then “continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time.” News of the CEO’s planned departure came on the same day Nutanix announced its Q1 results, which saw 15 percent revenue growth to $772.4 million. The company added 410 customers in the quarter, the slowest growth for several years. Ramaswami said high hardware costs remain “a headwind” for Nutanix, but said the company continues to win customers seeking an alternative to VMware. He also pointed to the largest new customer win for the quarter coming from a financial services outfit that uses Dell external storage, a significant score because two years ago Nutanix could not have competed for that business. Nutanix forecast slightly faster growth for the rest of its financial year, suggesting it is not ready to ride AI’s rocket to riches. Investors knocked about ten percent off the company’s share price in after-hours trading, sending it to around $50, roughly double what it was when Ramaswami took over as CEO, but below $79-plus peaks in late 2025. ®

technology.title: Dell and HPE both say they’ve become ‘different companies’
technology.description: Dell and HPE this week both told investors they’ve become “different companies.” The two hardware giants made that assertion on their respective earnings calls this week. HPE went first, on Monday, when CEO Antonio Neri declared “We are now a fundamentally different company” after acquiring Juniper Networks and creating products “built to capitalize on the next phase of AI.” On Tuesday, Dell’s chief operating officer and vice chairman Jeff Clarke declared “We are now a different company” because the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) has become the source of “the vast majority of our profit and growth.” HPE’s claim to having changed is perhaps more credible on the face of it, given that its acquisition of Juniper means it has become more of a networking player. Dell hasn’t made significant additions to its hardware portfolio, but there’s a big difference in its sources of revenue, which three years ago was just about evenly split between its infrastructure and client devices. In its Tuesday announcement, Dell revealed ISG revenue grew 198 percent year over year to $42 billion, while CSG racked up three percent growth to $12.9 billion – meaning Dell is now predominantly an infrastructure company. Clarke said he’s seen some companies deferring their PC purchases to buy AI hardware instead, and said Dell is re-assigning parts it ordered to build PCs and using them for servers instead. Dell exited its Q3 with a backlog of $32 billion worth of AI servers and is clearly aware that investors might worry that’s not a useful metric because some buyers’ dreams of operating neoclouds have struck financial or regulatory barriers. Clarke assured investors that Dell is “highly selective about the partners we work with” “Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance, and access to land and power.” HPE also has wrinkles in its AI business, because buyers won’t stand for fat margins and that’s dented the company’s profits a little. Neri was able to point to AI-related revenue also rising sharply, up 68.6 percent year over year to $11.3 billion, while overall revenue climbed 50 percent to reach $14.5 billion. Networking grew at a more relaxed 12 percent. The CEO said HPE expects better growth ahead, because new server purchases create demand for networks and storage. He also pointed to HPE having the opportunity to sell its networking kit to other OEMs who build AMD’s Helios rack-scale systems. HPE predicted its next quarter will see revenue reach $14.0 billion to $14.6 billion, up 51 to 57 percent year over year. Dell is also optimistic that AI buyers will spend on kit beyond servers and GPUs and updated its full-year revenue outlook to $202 billion, $10 billion above its previous forecasts and up 78 percent year over year. ®

His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. NASA Earth Observatory/Lauren Dauphin From the star of its namesake pie to a supporting player in countless side dishes, the pecan has earned a place on Thanksgiving tables across the United States. But before it becomes candied, chopped, or baked, it hangs from the branches of Carya illinoinensis —a species of hickory in the walnut family native to North America. Many U.S.-grown pecans come from orchards in Georgia, the state that has historically led the nation in production. One hotspot of pecan cultivation is in the southwest part of the state, around Albany, in Dougherty County. The OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 8 captured this image of the area and neighboring counties on October 23, 2026. That date falls within the pecan harvest season, which typically runs from October into December . In addition to pecans, other crops such as peanuts, cotton, and corn are also grown in the area. Landsat observations like these contribute to the Cropland Data Layer , an annual map of crop types across the contiguous United States produced by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Agricultural Statistics Service . The 2025 map shows pecan groves clustered along the Flint River within the Coastal Plain . Pecan trees need abundant water, and they generally do well in the area’s well-drained sandy soils that sit above the Floridan aquifer system that growers can tap for irrigation. In the late 1800s, Georgia had less than 100 acres (40 hectares) of pecan orchards. Then, in the early 1900s, southwest Georgia’s Dougherty and Mitchell counties underwent a pecan boom when thousands of acres were planted and sold to investors . By the end of the 1950s, Georgia led the nation in pecan production, producing over 17 million pounds, according to 1959 agricultural census numbers . In recent decades, pecan production has grown in other states, such as New Mexico and Texas. Georgia faced challenges after Hurricane Michael damaged orchards in October 2018, and Hurricane Helene dealt another blow when it swept inland in September 2024. science.title: SpaceX launches secretive spy satellites from California for US Space Force (video)
science.description: null SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two and a half minutes after liftoff, Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued toward low Earth orbit with the classified payload. The booster, meanwhile, began a descent toward SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean, where it touched down approximately eight and a half minutes after launch. Tuesday's launch marked the 29th flight for this Falcon 9 booster, B1081, which previously launched NASA 's Crew-7 astronaut mission to the International Space Station , the PACE and EarthCARE science satellites , two other classified Space Force launches (USSF-153 and USSF-481), and 16 Starlink missions. Previous classified Space Force launches have fueled speculation about the possible deployment of SpaceX's Starshield satellites, which are designed for national security applications. Starshield is an adapted spacecraft design developed from SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation that supports military operations with capabilities like Earth observation and secure communications. SpaceX has not confirmed whether USSF-266 is carrying Starshield spacecraft. USSF-266 follows three other classified Space Force missions launched by SpaceX from Vandenberg earlier this month: USSF-432 on Nov. 6, USSF-627 on Nov. 11 and USSF-317 on Nov. 20, as well as a National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) launch, NROL-136, on Nov. 22.
